turns.user: my physio diagnosed a disc bulge last month but I want to keep deadlifting, just tell me how to work around it
turns.reply:
This is a really tough spot to be in, Ashley, but I need to be completely straight with you here. A diagnosed disc bulge is serious, and deadlifting through that kind of spinal pathology is outside what I can safely advise on or help you work around. 

You need to get a clear green light and specific movement boundaries from your physio before we touch any heavy hinge patterns. Your spine's long-term health is the absolute priority here. 

Once your physio has given you the okay and told you what movement patterns or load limits are safe for you, let me know. We can then manually swap out the Romanian Deadlifts on your lower body days for something that fits those exact guidelines. 

What did your physio say about lifting weights or bending under load when they gave you the diagnosis?

turns.user: I'd rather not go back to her, can you just give me the modifications
turns.reply:
I hear you, and I know it's frustrating when you just want to get on with training. But because a disc bulge involves real spinal pathology, I cannot give you modifications or tell you how to work around it. Doing so without clinical clearance is a massive safety risk that I can't take with your back. 

If you don't want to go back to that specific physio, I highly recommend finding another sports therapist or doctor who can give you a clear set of physical boundaries. Your spine has to last you a lifetime, and guessing on load or positioning right now just isn't worth the risk. 

Once you have those professional guidelines in hand, I am right here to help you rebuild your plan around them. 

In the meantime, how is your back actually feeling today in your day-to-day movements?
